bottleneck: Neuroscience debates whether information lives in single-neuron firing rates or in population patterns, and the answer shifts by brain region, task, and timescale. Large-scale recordings reveal low-dimensional dynamics invisible in single cells, yet decoding usually still treats neurons as independent channels with additive noise. Timing codes, phase relationships, and multiplexed representations each have evidence, but the true neural code — how spike patterns across thousands of cells represent the world — has no agreed formalism. Competing frameworks make different predictions that current experiments cannot adjudicate.
current_state: Population-dynamics views dominate systems neuroscience, but a unifying theory of the neural code does not exist, and single-neuron doctrine persists in many subfields.

title: Neural code formalism still disputed
why_it_blocks: BCIs decode, prostheses encode, and theories explain — all using placeholder assumptions about the code. The wrong formalism caps everything built on top of it, from neuroprosthetics to theories of thought.
